name: Fasted cardio

lead: Fasted cardio means doing aerobic exercise before the day's first meal, typically first thing in the morning. It is a staple of bodybuilding-style cutting phases, used to lean out for a defined look.

Practitioners believe that exercising with low carbohydrate availability after an overnight fast shifts fuel use toward body fat. The sources reviewed contain no controlled trial comparing fasted with fed cardio, and the only related paper is a case report on bodybuilders' contest-preparation habits.

paras: Users do easy to moderate cardio, often walking or cycling for 20 to 60 minutes, right after waking and before breakfast, as part of a cutting phase.
No harms were documented in the sources reviewed. The one related paper involved bodybuilders whose routines also included heavy anabolic steroid use.

chain: More energy drawn from body fat
angle.text: Cardio before breakfast is used in bodybuilding cuts on the belief that low carbohydrate stores shift energy use toward body fat, helping you lean out. Direct research on it is limited.

lead: Fasted cardio is aerobic exercise done after an overnight fast, usually first thing in the morning before eating. It is a staple of bodybuilding-style cutting phases, where practitioners believe that exercising with low carbohydrate stores shifts energy use toward body fat, helping them get leaner and more defined for a contest or a physique goal [1][2].

In physique and looksmaxxing circles it is discussed as a way to lean out for a sharper jawline and visible muscle. T Nation members ask who is doing morning fasted cardio in cutting season, and one contest-prep log lists too much fasted cardio as a suspected cause of muscle loss, showing how lifters weigh it against keeping muscle [3][4].

Controlled studies exist. A 2014 four-week trial in 20 young women on a calorie-restricted diet found both fasted and fed aerobic groups lost weight and fat mass with no significant between-group differences [5]. Later studies have looked at appetite, energy balance and fat distribution after fasted exercise [6][7][8].

paras: In bodybuilding, competitors generally gain muscle in an off-season and then cut, eating below maintenance and adding cardiovascular exercise to lose fat before a contest [1]. Fasted cardio is a variant in which the session is done before any food that day. A 2017 case report and critical review interviewed six competitive bodybuilders and their coaches about the nutrition, drug and training strategies used in bulking and cutting phases, and compared them with scientific evidence [2].

Proponents say that with low liver glycogen and low insulin after an overnight fast, more fat is mobilized during exercise. A 2019 study of brisk walking in 12 men found blood fatty acids were higher when fasted, while carbohydrate oxidation and some gut hormones were higher when fed [6].

On T Nation, a poster in a 2021 transformation thread asks who is doing morning fasted cardio or conditioning [3]. In a contest prep log, a competitor lists too much fasted cardio, which he thinks probably led to muscle loss, among changes he would make, and notes his coach preferred low- and moderate-intensity cardio over HIIT in prep [4].

Schoenfeld and colleagues randomized 20 young women on a calorie-restricted diet to fasted or fed aerobic training for four weeks; both groups lost weight and fat mass with no significant between-group differences [5]. A 2024 study of 12 active adults found fasted and fed 75-minute runs produced no differences in energy intake, total energy expenditure, appetite or glucose over four days [7]. A 2025 pilot in people with type 2 diabetes who trained for 16 weeks found visceral and intramuscular fat fell more after fasted exercise, in a small sample, with no difference in liver fat [8].

lore.intro: Fasted cardio is discussed among lifters as a cutting tool and as something that might cost muscle if overdone [3][4].

claims.claim: Cardio on an empty stomach burns more fat and gets you leaner.
Too much fasted cardio can cost muscle.
